scope: Continue Triggerword-5 P0 effect forensics into the Realtime voice tool bridge, separating direct in-process UnifiedDB writes, custom voice confirmation, delegated Claude-Code execution, and shared EffectGate proof without executing or modifying the donor.

atoms.what_it_does: frank_erinnerung_schreiben routes to _tool_erinnerung_schreiben(), then _stern('gespraech-erinnerung-schreiben'). _stern imports stern in-process and directly calls stern.gespraech_erinnerung_schreiben(), which writes the dedicated gespraech_erinnerung table through schreib_verbindung(). This Realtime write path does not traverse Claude Code PreToolUse/PostToolUse and therefore does not use zulassen()/merken() effect-hook correlation.
atoms.why_it_exists: Give the live voice session low-latency durable conversation memory without subprocess/fork deadlocks while keeping the writer narrow.
atoms.failure_mode: If treated as equivalent to a canonical world-effect path, the architecture silently creates a second authority surface. The actual donor writer is narrow, but its admission/provenance semantics differ from normal hook-based tool effects.
atoms.concurrency_implication: SQLite writer semantics apply; there is no per-tool_use_id effect journal binding on this path.
atoms.privacy_implication: The path persists model-selected subject/value into durable memory; it is scoped to one table but requires explicit provenance/privacy policy in 2.0.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: In-process dispatch deliberately avoids the measured fork/subprocess latency/deadlock class.
known_counterevidence: Bypassing Claude Code hooks is not proof of unauthorized behavior under the donor design; memory writes and external world effects are different effect classes and should not be conflated.
open_questions: Define MEMORY_WRITE_ADMISSION separately from WORLD_EFFECT_ADMISSION while retaining one canonical state substrate and provenance law.

atoms.what_it_does: frank_auftrag_stellen executes nothing on the first model call. Dispatch requires a second call with exactly the same normalized Auftrag text, bestaetigt=true, at least one new server-originated input-audio transcription event, no keyword contradiction in intervening transcripts, and proposal age <=300 seconds. Only then does it call self.auftrag.stellen().
atoms.why_it_exists: Prevent one misheard or third-party utterance from directly dispatching an agentic job from voice.
outputs: proposal rejection/ASK state or asynchronous Auftrag dispatch
writes: background Auftrag queue on confirmed path
atoms.failure_mode: Source explicitly admits no speaker verification/diarization or full intent classification; an unrelated second utterance can still be misread as confirmation when keyword veto misses it.
atoms.concurrency_implication: One pending proposal slot is session-local; proposal replacement is explicit but not an immutable multi-request ledger.
atoms.privacy_implication: Uses transcript text and preserves recent transcript log in RAM for the check.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: Adds one human dialogue turn before real Auftrag dispatch.
known_counterevidence: The gate is stronger than model-only confirmation but intentionally incomplete for multi-speaker attribution.
open_questions: Bind proposal and confirmation to immutable audio/transcript causal IDs plus EffectRequest identity, not normalized text and counters alone.

atoms.what_it_does: Confirmed voice Auftrag is handed to _HintergrundBruecke -> _claude_taetigkeit -> gespraechsmodus.claude_frage(), which launches/resumes a real Claude Code -p session. The voice lane hard-disallows Bash via --disallowedTools while keeping file tools available. This is a distinct delegated execution stage after the voice confirmation gate.
atoms.why_it_exists: Keep low-latency voice separate from the slower action-capable Claude Code executor while preserving session continuity.
writes: whatever admitted Claude Code tools perform
atoms.failure_mode: Source inspection alone cannot prove which plugin hooks/settings are loaded for every spawned process; therefore this stage cannot be credited as canonical EffectGate enforcement merely because it is Claude Code.
atoms.concurrency_implication: Background tasks can overlap; downstream per-call identity must survive asynchronous delegation.
atoms.privacy_implication: Confirmed voice Auftrag text crosses into Claude Code prompt context.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: Asynchronous bridge avoids blocking live voice but decouples request time from eventual effect/outcome time.
atoms.state_lifetime: job/session scoped with later result re-entry
known_counterevidence: Normal Claude Code hooks may load in this spawned process; exact current hook reachability/order was not established in this packet.
open_questions: Prove exact hook loading/order for the spawned command or move canonical enforcement below both voice and Claude Code so correctness does not depend on plugin lifecycle configuration.

atoms.what_it_does: Current donor behavior is split across nonblocking stern hook bookkeeping for normal Claude Code tools, a voice-specific two-step confirmation before delegated Auftrag dispatch, direct in-process stern writes for Realtime memory, and the historically separate wache-koenig blocker. These are donor primitives with different scopes, not one source-proven current cross-modal EffectGate.
atoms.why_it_exists: The architecture evolved incrementally around different latency, modality and safety problems.
writes: multiple typed and legacy state surfaces
atoms.failure_mode: Calling all of these 'EffectGate' hides distinct semantics and can turn request, confirmation, dispatch and observed success into one ambiguous status.
atoms.concurrency_implication: Cross-surface identity is not structurally unified in donor source.
atoms.privacy_implication: Different paths expose different data; a single typed authority contract must retain modality-specific privacy controls.
atoms.latency_or_cost_implication: Convergence must preserve the low-latency in-process voice path rather than reintroducing subprocess deadlocks.
known_counterevidence: Different operation classes legitimately need different front-gates; convergence means one canonical typed authority/provenance and real-effect path, not identical policy semantics for reads, memories and world effects.
open_questions: Define modality-specific front gates that compile into one EffectRequest/EffectDecision identity before the final executor boundary.

hypotheses: Frankenstein 2.0 should compile voice confirmation into a typed EffectRequest/EffectDecision, then require the same immutable effect identity at the final executor and EffectJournal regardless of whether the request originated in text, voice, GRID or another modality.

Direct Realtime memory writes can remain fast/local if they are narrow typed state writes with explicit source/causal identity and deterministic admission, but they must not become a second canonical authority.
counterhypotheses: The delegated Claude Code process may already load normal plugin hooks. Even if true, normal stern.zulassen() is source-proven nonblocking, so current final enforcement still requires exact proof.

The voice confirmation gate is intentionally stronger than generic text admission and should remain modality-specific; shared authority can be achieved at the typed effect identity/executor layer without weakening that front gate.
contradictions: TW5-CONTRADICTION-REALTIME-EFFECT-AUTHORITY-007: current donor voice/tool architecture has multiple write/action control surfaces with different semantics and no source-proven single current enforcement boundary across them; do not claim EffectGate already covers Realtime end-to-end.
critical_unknowns: Exact hook/plugin/settings reachability of the Claude Code process spawned by gespraechsmodus.claude_frage().
Current-host installation/order/reachability of the now-pinned historical wache-koenig predecessor.
Any direct Realtime writer beyond dedicated conversation memory that can cause world effects without the two-step Auftrag gate.
Exact causal identity mapping Realtime call_id/transcript/audio event -> proposal -> confirmation -> Claude tool_use_id -> effect_id -> outcome receipt.

recommended_next_spans.reason: Resolve exact spawned command, permission and hook/settings reachability.
Bind or falsify current wache-koenig installation and ordering without using historical source identity as runtime credit.
Map direct voice memory admission/provenance into typed state-write contract.
